title: Scheduler misrank causing hotpath kernel thrashing and p99 latency spikes
creator: Alex Kim
description: Summary: During a mid-week capacity burst we observed a correlated p95/p99 latency regression for chat endpoints backed by the v2-attn optimized kernels. The runtime's scheduler began misranking candidate kernels under load leading to hotpath thrashing: frequent kernel reassignments, micro-evictions of KV cache, and degraded batching efficiency. This ticket tracks the investigation notes, temporary mitigations, and concrete action items to prevent recurrence.

investigation_summary: Root cause: a scheduler heuristic change merged in release runtime-1.21 reduced the score penalty for speculative kernel probes while simultaneously lowering the dampening window. Under bursty, multi-tenant arrival patterns that spike short-lived high-concurrency microbursts, the scheduler began to issue aggressive kernel probes. Probes caused kernel candidate ranking flaps: workers repeatedly switched kernels mid-session which invalidated warm KV cache entries and prevented stable batching. This amplified tail latency due to repeated kernel reinitialization (context switches, kernel codepaths) and increased backend contention.
mitigation: Immediate: Increased probe backoff and restored previous hysteresis constants for canary and primary regions. Added temporary circuit-breaker that suppresses probing when per-worker kernel-switch rate > 3 switches/min. Medium-term: Canary rollout of deterministic scoring (score = static_rank + congestion_penalty + probe_suppression) to avoid equal-scoring ties that previously led to oscillation. We also added KV cache eviction metrics and per-worker kernel-switch counters to tracing.
root_cause: The combination of two changes (probe aggressiveness + reduced dampening) created a brittle scheduling surface under realistic burst distributions. The scheduler's tie-breaking used non-deterministic iteration order over candidate lists; when multiple candidates had near-identical scores the order depended on hashmap iteration which varied with runtime allocations. This allowed small timing jitter to flip kernel assignment decisions repeatedly.
